The Intercept Brasil.titulo: U.S. Website Gave False Approval to Green Card Applicants — Then Blamed Glitch and Took It Away
The Intercept Brasil.resumoOriginal:
When Jesse Miranda, a U.S. citizen, sponsored an application for a green card for his wife nearly a year ago, he understood the process would take time.



On Wednesday, when he saw someone posting on Reddit that they had received sudden approval for a loved one’s initial application for permanent residence, he wondered if he and his wife had gotten lucky.



Miranda quickly went to check the application status on the website of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, the agency that oversees visas and naturalization.



“What kind of glitch causes these mass approvals?”



To his delight, the portal showed that their application had also been approved to move on to the next step in the process. Yet he had a nagging suspicion: Was this coming too soon? Wait times for approval of just the first step in the process can stretch more than two years, so could his wife’s application really be getting moved along so quickly?



When he called the agency’s helpline Thursday morning to confirm the approval, his suspicions proved correct. Miranda said the employee answering his call told him that his wife’s application status was unchanged.



And they weren’t the only people affected: According to Miranda, the employee acknowledged that USCIS was aware of a glitch affecting numerous applicants.



“It was heartbreaking,” Miranda told The Intercept of learning that their application status had not in fact changed. “I get that there’s technical stuff behind the scenes, but at the same time, what kind of glitch causes these mass approvals?”







The apparent glitch resulted in dozens or more applicants for green cards receiving false notices of approval for a key step in the process, according to multiple people who received the false approvals and accounts of similar approvals posted online. (USCIS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.)



In addition to Miranda, The Intercept spoke with two other green card applicants who received false notices of approval for the I-130 form, the first major hurdle in the process for obtaining a permanent residency visa for relatives of a U.S. citizen.



Dozens more people on Reddit and a user on an immigration-related Discord server reported experiencing the same false approval notices when they checked their application status on Wednesday and Thursday.



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      Trump Wants Immigrants on U.S. Soil to Hand Over Social Media Accounts to Apply for Citizenship
    
    
  



People began to report on immigration forums on Wednesday that they’d received approval the I-130 form, but elation turned to devastation as they came to understand the notices as an error.



On Thursday, the USCIS site appeared to be down for a time. When it came back up, accounts for applications of at least two of the people who spoke to The Intercept still showed their loved ones’ green cards as being “approved.”



Americans’ Loved Ones



The I-130 form is just the first step in applying for a green card for the spouse or relative of a U.S. citizen.



Wait times for the form’s approval range, on average, between 10 and 20 months. Often, however, they stretch out to two years or more. During that time, the applicant is unable to live or work in the U.S.



Approval, then, is the first sign that couples or families are one step closer to living their lives together in the U.S.



“This feeling of not having your partner here is already painful enough,” Miranda said. “It’s even more painful when you have that approval waved in your face, only to have your dreams crushed.”



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      Trump’s National Killer Police Force
    
    
  



Kate, an American citizen whose spouse and stepchild have applications pending, told The Intercept she saw an erroneous approval notice for her case on the USCIS website on Thursday after reading online posts about a flurry of approvals overnight.



Kate, who spoke with The Intercept on the condition that her surname and certain identifying details be withheld for fear of affecting her spouse’s immigration process, said she and her partner and stepchild had applied for the I-130 nearly a year ago and are living apart from one another as they await approval. 



“I don’t know how I’m going to tell him. He’s going to be devastated.”



She happened to be visiting her spouse’s country of origin, and they were thrilled to be able to celebrate the milestone of being one step closer to a green card together. When she got back from their celebratory lunch, however, she checked the site again and found that none of the usual signifiers of an approval were showing up, including an approval notice that would usually appear in the site’s documents tab.



She said she had not yet told her spouse that the approval appeared to be the result of a glitch.



“It’s just devastating,” she said. “I don’t know how I’m going to tell him. He’s going to be devastated.”



    
              
                  
            
                  
            Read Our Complete Coverage          
        
        The War on Immigrants
      
    
  


“Straight Up Unfair”



On a Reddit forum dedicated to the pain and suffering of the I-130 process — called “r/I130Suffering” — dozens of people reported similar experiences with the glitch, starting with sudden elation and ending more demoralized than ever.



And on Track My Visa, a Discord where applicants swap advice and gripes about the immigration process, numerous users reported the same. On Thursday, the moderators of the forum suspended a channel dedicated to celebrating approval notices lest people celebrate prematurely.







The glitch is just the latest frustration for Miranda, who said the process to bring his wife to the U.S. has been so fraught that it’s forced a reassessment of long-held political beliefs.



The son of Mexican immigrants who immigrated legally and ultimately received citizenship, Miranda said he had long considered himself a Republican and felt that tough immigration policy was necessary to ensure a fair shot to people immigrating legally.



Now, he said, seeing how difficult it is to immigrate legally, even as the spouse of a citizen, he’s wondering if he had it wrong.



“I always thought ‘they’re just going after illegals,’” he said. “But this is affecting legal immigration to the point where it’s almost stopped. You can have a million dollars and get a green card, but if you’re trying to process a loved one and you can’t — that’s just straight up unfair.”
The post U.S. Website Gave False Approval to Green Card Applicants — Then Blamed Glitch and Took It Away appeared first on The Intercept.

The Intercept Brasil.titulo: Trump’s Crypto Corruption Puts Centrist Democrats in Bind
The Intercept Brasil.resumoOriginal:
The latest version of a sweeping crypto bill exposed a deep divide between progressives and moderate Senate Democrats: whether to accommodate the industry ahead of the fall midterms, or declare open war on it.



Seven Democrats issued a statement Wednesday night lamenting that they cannot vote for the latest draft of the bill, citing weak provisions aimed at tamping down Donald Trump’s crypto self-enrichment, among other issues. In a joint statement, they pledged to keep working with Republicans to “get this over the finish line.”



Other Democrats say they have had enough of crypto, however. The problems with the bill run much deeper than Trump’s corruption, Sen. Chris Murphy, D-Conn., said at a Wednesday speech, and it is time for Democrats to openly break with the industry and its $189 million in campaign funds.



“This bill is in front of the Senate because the industry paid for it,” Murphy said. “We should, in this election, make crypto’s purchase of our political process, AI’s purchase of our political process, a major campaign issue.”



“This bill is in front of the Senate because the industry paid for it.”



The two sides staked out their position as Republicans released a draft text of the far-reaching bill known as the Clarity Act, which would create an industry-friendly regulatory structure for cryptocurrencies.



Critics say there are many problems with the bill, including lax consumer protections and loopholes that would enable money laundering. Nothing in the monthslong fight over the legislation has generated as much controversy as Trump’s self-dealing, however.



Between the $TRUMP meme coin and other ventures, Trump profited at least $1.4 billion off crypto last year. Democrats have proposed requiring Trump to divest himself of his crypto ventures and put enforcement in the hands of Democratic state attorneys general.



Instead, Republicans issued a proposal, with Trump’s blessing, that would prevent him from issuing new meme coins and put enforcement in the hands of his own Department of Justice and would not be enforceable after he leaves office.



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand Wants to Save Crypto — But Trump Windfall Is a Political Obstacle
    
    
  



No matter what’s in the legislation, the bill is meaningless if it leaves enforcement to Trump’s own administration, said Mark Hays, the associate director for cryptocurrency and financial technology at Americans for Financial Reform and Demand Progress.



“I don’t think anybody who is following the DOJ seriously thinks they will do that,” he said. “That is just not how this administration works.”







Even Sen. Adam Schiff, a California Democrat who has often sided with crypto in the past, said he opposes the language in the bill addressing Trump. Schiff told reporters at the Capitol that that text gives the appearance it applies to Trump and his family without actually doing so.



“It’s a complete nonstarter,” he said.



The bill’s flaws led the seven mostly centrist Democrats to issue a statement hours after the release of the draft text saying that they could not vote for it in its current form.



“Key provisions including those addressing ethics for elected officials, consumer protection, illicit finance, conflicts of interest and market integrity must be strengthened. We have been working in good faith with our Republican colleagues for the past year and will continue doing so to get this over the finish line,” said the group, which included Sen. Angela Alsobrooks, D-Md., one of the top negotiators on the bill.







The time for Democrats and Republicans to reach a compromise is slipping fast, however. The Senate goes into recess on August 7, and few observers expect Congress to take the measure up again as the midterms approach.



Senate Majority Leader John Thune said that he hopes to put the measure to a vote before senators leave town.



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      Who’s Spending in Your Congressional Election? We Tracked the Front Groups Fueling the 2026 Midterms.
    
    
  



Democrats are nervously eying the industry’s war chest if they are put on the record as opposing the Clarity Act. Companies including Coinbase, the largest publicly traded crypto company, have contributed $189 million into super PACs and candidate campaign funds to influence the midterms.



In the past, some of the spending has benefited Democrats such as Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz. Yet it may have also contributed to Democrats losing the Senate in 2024.



Murphy, in the Wednesday speech at the Center for American Progress, said it would be better to attack the industry than try to work with it.



“They are spending money in order to get a pro-crypto bill passed through the United States Senate and House of Representatives,” Murphy said. “And there are, I guess, two approaches that the Democratic Party could take. One approach is to just do what the crypto industry wants and then cross our fingers and hope they don’t spend money against us in the next election. Good luck with that strategy. The second approach is to make the industry’s brazen attempts to buy our political process a campaign issue.”
The post Trump’s Crypto Corruption Puts Centrist Democrats in Bind appeared first on The Intercept.

The Intercept Brasil.titulo: On a West Bank Eviction Tour, Israeli Settlers Advertise “No Arabs Here”
The Intercept Brasil.resumoOriginal:
WEST BANK — On a hillside overlooking the Palestinian village of al-Mughayyir, a crowd of Israelis and Jewish visitors from abroad gathered for an inside look at how settlement works. They listened intently as Netanel, an Israeli settler-soldier in olive fatigues with a rifle strapped to his back, advertised his group’s impact in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.



“It started with this hilltop,” he said, referring to the current settlement push that has crept ever closer to al-Mughayyir. “We ended up putting the area in Jewish hands. There are no Arabs here.”



Netanel was speaking on a tour aimed at English-speaking Jews, some of whom expressed interest in moving to the settlements. He described his “mission” to support his fellow settlers and shepherds in their return to “Judea and Samaria,” the biblical name Israeli settlers and the Israeli government use for the West Bank.



The settlement movement is accelerating, recruiting outsiders to join and bringing in reinforcements from the military’s Hagmar battalions, regional defense units staffed largely with settlement residents that have exploded in size since October 7, 2023. The government has issued thousands of rifles to civilian security squads, at times distributed personally by Israel’s far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir. Israeli watchdog groups describe the push as an unprecedented state-backed land grab, one that settlers are carrying out with an odd combination of tools: government-supplied rifles alongside herds of sheep and goats.



Reservist settler-soldiers like the Hagmar battalions “are not simply self-organized militia groups,” said Marko Milanovic, a professor of public international law at the University of Reading. “In essence, they should be treated in the same way as IDF soldiers as a legal matter.”



Established in 2025, the Metzudat David is illegal, even under Israeli law. It is one of 10 Israeli outposts that now surround al-Mughayyir as settlements expand at a rapid clip in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. At one stop on the tour, a group of Israeli youths could be seen building a new housing unit for a family slated to move into the settlement.



“The ultimate goal is for people to leave their homes and villages. But the settlers aren’t acting alone, they’re backed by the Israeli government, which uses them as instruments to get what it wants,” Amin Abu Alia, the council head of al-Mughayyir, told The Intercept.



Settlers have taken over more than 38,000 dunams of al-Mughayyir’s grazing and farmland, the equivalent of nearly 9,400 acres. Across the West Bank, settlers living in farm outposts now effectively control roughly 1 million dunams — nearly a fifth of the entire territory — according to a report published this month by the Israeli watchdog groups Peace Now and Kerem Navot. The report found that roughly 750,000 of those dunams were seized since the current Israeli government took office in late 2022.



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      Armed Israeli Settlers Detained Ro Khanna. He Wants Their Illegal Outposts Demolished.
    
    
  



Of al-Mughayyir’s roughly 41,000 dunams, Palestinians today have practical access to only 1,200 to 1,500, Abu Alia said. The village’s eastern gate, which opens onto the Alon Road, has been closed by the Israeli military since 2023. 



In response to questions from The Intercept, COGAT, the Israeli defense body that administers the West Bank, said the outposts “are known to the Civil Administration and are unauthorized.” The COGAT spokesperson added that the body had already demolished other unauthorized settlement structures. “Additional enforcement measures will be taken in accordance with enforcement priorities, the operational situation assessment, and the approval of the political echelon,” the spokesperson said.



“Once [the Metzudat David] outpost went in, it effectively closed off the village’s access to land to the east, displacing the community from that land,” Dror Etkes, the head of the Israeli settlement watchdog Kerem Navot, told The Intercept. Residents describe a growing sense of foreboding, a feeling that their time is running short before life in al-Mughayyir becomes untenable. And that fear has only grown. On Saturday, a 17-year-old resident, Fadi Naasan, died of wounds he sustained when he was shot during a raid on the village earlier that month, according to the al-Mughayyir village council.




    
      
      The Maoz Esther settlement in the northern West Bank. Photo: Theia Chatelle/The Intercept    
    



Only a handful of settlers like Netanel oversee the Metzudat David outpost. Otherwise, dozens of animals fan out across the land to claim as much space as possible, requiring very little manpower.



On the tour in June, Netanel showed off the more than 100 sheep and goats that do the settlers’ work for them. The herds graze out Palestinian crops, and their steady, intimidating presence — backed by the threat of settler violence — pushes farmers off land they can no longer safely use, clearing the way for the outpost to absorb it.      



These outposts now control at least 786,000 dunams, roughly 14 percent of all land in the West Bank. Some 70 percent of the land seized by grazing outposts was taken in the past few years, according to Kerem Navot and Peace Now.



For now, the settlers don’t make any money from the livestock, Netanel said. The milk and meat aren’t profitable, but “the other work they do,” he said, “is invaluable.”



Palestinians living in al-Mughayyir are unable to enter the Alon Road, the main artery connecting the eastern half of the West Bank, and must exit through the western side of the village, via Khirbet Abu Falah. Residents say this adds at least an hour to any trip.



Even the fallback route is under threat. One of the new outposts, built inside Area B on al-Mughayyir’s northwestern lands, also encroaches on the very villages the detour runs through, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.



“They can do whatever they want. You can’t do anything about it.”



“If you go through the IDF checkpoint, it’s a gamble. They can arrest you, beat you, steal your money, steal your belongings,” Omar Mohammed, who lives in al-Mughayyir, told The Intercept. “They can do whatever they want. You can’t do anything about it.” The Israeli military did not respond to questions about mistreatment of residents at checkpoints.







Hodaya, who led the tour and knew a reporter was present, gave only her first name, like Netanel. “On the other side of two hills, there are also another settlement,” she said. “So now, you know, the [farms] are surrounded by Jews, and that helps to make the place more safe.”



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      Trump’s Sanctions Against the ICC Are Unconstitutional, Rights Groups Say
    
    
  



During the tour, an Israeli military armored personnel carrier was stationed at the village’s yellow gate — the kind that has become a distinct marker of movement restrictions across the West Bank since October 7, 2023 — was shut.



When one of the participants on the tour asked whether Palestinians resisted attempts to confiscate their land, Hodaya answered, “They don’t accept it and say, ‘Oh, very nice, we’re going away.’ Of course they’ll fight. They’re on the land, and they were permanent … but they understand that there’s a change.”



There was a sense of excitement on the tour about a Jewish return to what participants called Judea and Samaria, and an explicit recognition that doing so would require displacing Palestinians from their land.     “The assumption is that ‘We cannot get rid of [the roughly 3 million] Palestinians right now in the West Bank,’” Etkes, of the watchdog group Kerem Navot, said, describing the settler thinking. “‘So what we have to do is isolate them and take from them their means of livelihood.’”




    
      
      A Third Temple flag flies in the Maoz Esther settlement. The Hebrew text reads, “And they shall make me a sanctuary.” Photo: Theia Chatelle/The Intercept    
    



Al-Mughayyir was the village most affected by settler violence in the West Bank in 2025, when there were more than 70 recorded settler-related incidents, according to Nasser Khoudr, Middle East assistant research manager at the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data, known as ACLED. It is on track to earn the same distinction in 2026.



“One of the main reasons behind this is the expansion of nearby settlements and farming outposts, especially since 7 October,” Khoudr said. “This expansion has gone together with Israeli government policies that gave more power to settler security structures.”



In April, a settler shot and killed Aws al-Naasan, a 14-year-old student, and Jihad Abu Naim, a 32-year-old parent, at the boys’ school in al-Mughayyir, according to the United Nations and village officials.    



Video of the attack, verified by multiple news outlets, shows a man in military fatigues advancing on the village and firing repeatedly toward the school.



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      American Nurse Who Tried to Save “No Other Land” Activist Was Detained and Deported by Israel
    
    
  



The Israeli military said the shooter was a reservist traveling in a car with other Israeli civilians who exited the vehicle and opened fire at “suspects in the area,” alleging that they had thrown stones at the car. The military said the reservist was dismissed from reserve duty and his weapon confiscated, and that military police are reviewing the killings. No one has been arrested for the shooting.



Mohammed was one of the first to reach his friend’s body after the settler-reservist shot Aws in the head. “They come in half uniform, wearing the green pants, but not the shirt,” Mohammed said. “We can’t tell if they are a settler, a soldier, or, well, both.”



The distinction has dissolved. Even in regular army units, settler ideology has taken root. In March, reservists detained CNN correspondent Jeremy Diamond and his crew in the village of Tayasir while guarding an illegal outpost, telling the journalists on camera that the entire West Bank belongs to Jews and that they were avenging a settler’s death.



“We can’t tell if they are a settler, a soldier, or both.”



According to the U.N., no Israeli soldier has served prison time for killing a Palestinian in the West Bank since at least 2017, and the Israeli rights group Yesh Din found that 93.6 percent of investigations into settler violence between 2005 and 2025 were closed without indictments.



Last August, after a Palestinian gunman allegedly opened fire on a settler grazing his sheep on al-Mughayyir’s land, the Israeli military declared a closed military zone and uprooted olive trees across roughly 74 acres of the village’s land — at least 3,100 trees by the military’s own count, and far more according to village officials who spoke with The Intercept.



The military said that the clearing was necessary because vegetation near the road obstructed “the identification of enemy movement.” But the head of the army’s Central Command, Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, told troops the village would “pay a heavy price,” prompting two Israeli human rights groups to demand a criminal investigation into him, suspecting he was ordering collective punishment. None ever occurred.



Netanel described participating in the uprooting. He said it was sad to see the olive trees die, but “it is for security, security of this outpost. We need a clear line of sight into the land.” As Netanel spoke, the roots of the trees still pointed up into the air.



“It’s a process, a process that we are progressing,” Netanel said. “That’s what’s happening here.”



Update: July 23, 2026, 12:16 p.m. ETThis story has been updated with a comment from COGAT, the Israeli defense body that administers the West Bank.




The post On a West Bank Eviction Tour, Israeli Settlers Advertise “No Arabs Here” appeared first on The Intercept.

The Intercept Brasil.titulo: GOP Rep. Called Israeli–U.S. Defense Tech Integration “Dangerous.” The House Passed It Anyway.
The Intercept Brasil.resumoOriginal:
The House passed a $1.15 trillion defense authorization bill Wednesday with a controversial provision expanding U.S.-Israel military technology cooperation intact, despite a bipartisan effort to remove it and warnings from Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., that the measure could compromise American sovereignty and national security.



The 216–212 vote on the fiscal year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act passed mostly along party lines after lawmakers were denied a separate vote to remove Section 219, which would create a permanent initiative to merge U.S. and Israeli defense tech.



“Codifying the integration of our military technology and supply chains with those of any other country is dangerous,” said Massie, one of seven Republicans to buck party lines and vote against the NDAA. He was joined by Reps. Josh Brecheen of Oklahoma; Tim Burchett of Tennessee; Eli Crane of Arizona; Harriet Hageman of Wyoming; Anna Paulina Luna of Florida; and Chip Roy of Texas.



Six Democrats voted for it: Reps. Henry Cuellar of Texas; Don Davis of North Carolina; Jared Golden of Maine; Vicente Gonzalez of Texas; Adam Gray of California; and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington.



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      Congress Is Trying to Permanently Integrate U.S. and Israeli Defense Tech
    
    
  



Section 219 would establish a United States–Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative and require the defense secretary to designate a Pentagon executive agent responsible for coordinating bilateral defense research, development, testing, evaluation, and industrial cooperation.







Massie, who sought to remove the provision alongside Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., told The Intercept ahead of the vote that institutionalizing the relationship would create long-term national security risks.



Doing so with Israel would create “a lopsided arrangement” in which American national security is unnecessarily compromised, he added. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., similarly referred to the provision as “an existential threat to American sovereignty and democracy,” in a statement on social media.



Massie also pointed out that codifying the initiative would make it more difficult for future presidents to withdraw from the arrangement.



“Enshrining this broad agreement and the permanent position it creates in legislation removes the flexibility of future Presidents to withdraw from such an arrangement,” Massie said. He further argued that it “requires a treaty to effect, not an amendment buried in a law as presented here.”







The provision, previously numbered Section 224, has generated controversy since The Intercept reported on it in June. The Intercept found that it closely resembled the U.S.–Israel FUTURES Act, introduced by Reps. Ronny Jackson, R-Texas, and Davis, with companion legislation from Sens. Ted Budd, R-N.C., and Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y. All four lawmakers have received substantial campaign support from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee and other pro-Israel groups, while the FUTURES Act itself received public backing from AIPAC and the neoconservative foreign policy think tank FDD Action. Massie lost his primary for reelection to his Kentucky House seat in the spring, after President Donald Trump and AIPAC both backed his opponent.



The standalone FUTURES Act did not advance, but many of its core concepts subsequently appeared in the NDAA.



Massie and Khanna later led an amendment to strike Section 219, joined by Democratic Reps. Jim McGovern of Massachusetts; Jesús “Chuy” García of Illinois; Rashida Tlaib of Michigan; Don Beyer of Virginia; Jill Tokuda of Hawaii; Derek Tran of California; and Joe Courtney of Connecticut. The amendment was not made eligible for floor consideration. Luna, the Florida Republican, separately sought to strike Section 219, but her amendment was also denied a vote.



Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., rejected Massie’s sovereignty concerns.



“There is no world that the United States government gives away our most elite military weaponry or technology to our allies, including Israel,” Stutzman told The Intercept. “Just because we are collaborating with our allies to work towards a common goal of safe citizens doesn’t mean we are giving away American sovereignty.”



  
    
                          
      
        Related      
      Trump’s Formula for Forever Wars
    
    
  



Stutzman’s office previously told this reporter that Section 219, then numbered Section 224, originated with Jackson’s office. Stutzman separately told Responsible Statecraft that his own proposal to replace direct U.S. military assistance to Israel with trade and defense cooperation grew out of conversations with Israeli contacts.



Also on Wednesday, House Republicans passed a $95 billion budget plan to fund the war on Iran and impose new restrictions on elections.



House passage does not make Section 219 law. The Senate’s version of the NDAA, which has yet to pass, contains its own version of the defense technology initiative, leaving the proposal’s ultimate fate dependent on further Senate action and negotiations between the chambers.
The post GOP Rep. Called Israeli–U.S. Defense Tech Integration “Dangerous.” The House Passed It Anyway. appeared first on The Intercept.

DCM.titulo: VÍDEO: Netanyahu entra na campanha e chama Flávio Bolsonaro de “campeão do Brasil”
DCM.resumoOriginal:
O candidato a presidência Flávio Bolsonaro, e Benjamin Netanyahu em encontro realizado em janeiro desse ano. Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais
O primeiro-ministro de Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu, entrou oficialmente na campanha presidencial brasileira neste sábado (25). Em um vídeo exibido durante a convenção nacional do PL, em São Paulo, ele parabenizou Flávio Bolsonaro pelo lançamento da candidatura e chamou o senador de “grande campeão do Brasil”.
“Flávio, meu amigo. Quero parabenizá-lo pelo lançamento oficial de sua campanha. Você é um grande campeão do Brasil, é um grande defensor da amizade entre os nossos povos, e sei que levará o Brasil a patamares cada vez mais altos. Parabéns”, declarou Netanyahu, em inglês.
Flávio iniciou sua pré-campanha internacional com uma viagem a Israel em janeiro, acompanhado do irmão Eduardo Bolsonaro. Durante a visita, foi recebido por Netanyahu, participou de uma conferência organizada pelo governo israelense e acusou Lula de antissemitismo.

🇮🇱🇧🇷 NETANYAHU JOINS FLÁVIO’S CAMPAIGN WITH A MESSAGE OF SUPPORT
Thank you, Prime Minister @netanyahu.
Your words inspire millions who believe in freedom. Let’s make Brazil safer, stronger, and sweep evil out of our country. pic.twitter.com/ha3MAS3gNs
— Eduardo Bolsonaro🇧🇷 (@BolsonaroSP) July 25, 2026

Nos meses seguintes, o senador aprofundou as promessas de alinhamento. Flávio defendeu a transferência da Embaixada do Brasil de Tel Aviv para Jerusalém, medida prometida e nunca cumprida pelo governo de Jair Bolsonaro, e anunciou que pretende retirar o país de iniciativas internacionais contrárias ao governo israelense. Também prometeu reconhecer imediatamente um novo embaixador de Israel em Brasília.
O apoio é dado por um líder contra quem o Tribunal Penal Internacional mantém um mandado de prisão por crimes de guerra e crimes contra a humanidade na Faixa de Gaza. Entre as acusações estão o uso da fome como método de guerra, perseguição e outros atos desumanos. Netanyahu e o governo israelense rejeitam as acusações e contestam a jurisdição do tribunal.

DCM.titulo: VÍDEO – Lula reage à tentativa de interferência dos EUA: “Não venham meter o dedo nas nossas eleições”
DCM.resumoOriginal:
O presidente e candidato a reeleição, Lula (PT). Foto: Divulgação/Ricardo Stuckert
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva afirmou neste sábado (25) que qualquer tentativa estrangeira de interferir nas eleições brasileiras enfrentará uma reação dura do país. “Quem quiser de fora se meter nas eleições brasileiras vai apanhar muito aqui nas eleições”, declarou durante a convenção estadual do PT em Campinas.
“Que não venha ninguém de fora querer meter o dedo nas nossas eleições”, acrescentou Lula. O presidente afirmou que o destino do país será decidido pelos 157 milhões de eleitores brasileiros e reforçou que nenhuma autoridade estrangeira terá o direito de questionar ou dirigir o processo eleitoral.
A declaração ocorreu um dia depois de o Itamaraty negar vistos a Riley M. Barnes e Samuel Samson, dois integrantes do Departamento de Estado dos Estados Unidos que pretendiam viajar a Brasília para tratar do sistema eleitoral brasileiro. A missão foi descrita por autoridades brasileiras como inusitada e politicamente sensível.
Segundo apuração do jornal The Washington Post, Barnes e Samson pretendiam levantar dúvidas sobre a integridade das urnas poucas semanas antes da votação. Autoridades ouvidas pela agência avaliaram que a iniciativa buscava influenciar o ambiente político e enfraquecer a confiança nas eleições.

Lula acaba de mandar recado pro Trump que tava entalado na garganta de muito brasileiro.
“Quem quiser vir de fora se meter na eleição brasileira já fica avisado: VAI APANHAR MUITO. Quem decide o destino deste país são 157 milhões de eleitores. O Brasil é soberano. Este país é… pic.twitter.com/EQQXZH0RM2
— Bruno Guzzo® (@brunoguzzo) July 25, 2026
A ofensiva ocorre no momento em que Flávio Bolsonaro tenta reabrir a campanha de desinformação contra o sistema eletrônico de votação. Em reunião recente com representantes de dezenas de países, o senador afirmou falsamente que as urnas brasileiras seriam produzidas pela empresa venezuelana Smartmatic. A companhia e o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral negaram qualquer participação dela na fabricação dos equipamentos.
“O aviso está dado: o Brasil é soberano”, afirmou Lula. “O Brasil quer manter relações com todos os países do mundo. O Brasil não quer guerra, o Brasil quer paz. O Brasil não quer ódio, o Brasil quer amor. O Brasil não quer fazer futrica, o Brasil quer trabalhar.”
A fala foi feita durante a convenção que oficializou Fernando Haddad como candidato do PT ao governo de São Paulo. No palco, Lula também exaltou a chapa formada por Haddad, Márcio França, Marina Silva e Simone Tebet, mas transformou a defesa da soberania e das urnas em um dos principais eixos de seu discurso.

DCM.titulo: VÍDEO: Bolsonaro de IA critica Judiciário em evento de Flávio e levanta questionamentos jurídicos
DCM.resumoOriginal:
O candidato a presidência Flávio Bolsonaro, em evento de seu lançamento ao planalto. Foto: Jean Carniel/Reuters
Jair Bolsonaro não estava na convenção que oficializou a candidatura presidencial de Flávio Bolsonaro, mas o PL colocou uma versão artificial do ex-presidente no telão. Um vídeo produzido com inteligência artificial recriou sua imagem e sua voz para transmitir um pronunciamento de apoio ao filho neste sábado (25), em São Paulo.
“Estou preso e calado por uma decisão arbitrária”, declarou o Bolsonaro sintético. Na sequência, a gravação afirmou que “nenhuma prisão” poderia interromper o movimento político comandado pelo ex-presidente e pediu aos apoiadores que recebessem Flávio “de braços abertos” como candidato à Presidência.
Jair Bolsonaro cumpre prisão domiciliar e está proibido de usar telefone ou redes sociais, diretamente ou por intermédio de terceiros. Em julho, Alexandre de Moraes também vetou a divulgação de manifestações político-eleitorais do ex-presidente por outras pessoas até o fim da eleição. É o caso de se perguntar: é legal atribuir ao condenado uma falação ainda que seja artificial?

Vídeo de Jair Bolsonaro feito por Inteligência Artificial é exibido na convenção do PL pic.twitter.com/F7NZnZiJRe
— Sam Pancher (@SamPancher) July 25, 2026
A restrição foi ampliada depois que Flávio leu nas redes uma carta escrita pelo pai com um apelo pela união da direita em torno de sua candidatura. Moraes considerou que o senador havia servido como canal para uma comunicação proibida, suspendeu suas visitas ao pai por 90 dias e determinou a investigação de possível propaganda eleitoral antecipada.
Duas semanas depois, o PL voltou a transmitir essencialmente o mesmo recado, mas substituiu o papel manuscrito por uma réplica digital de Bolsonaro. A peça não apresentou apenas fotografias ou imagens ilustrativas: simulou o ex-presidente falando diretamente ao público e defendendo a candidatura de Flávio, como se estivesse participando da convenção.
O vídeo também pode abrir uma discussão na Justiça Eleitoral. A resolução do TSE para a eleição de 2026 obriga campanhas e partidos a identificarem de maneira explícita qualquer conteúdo sintético produzido por inteligência artificial. A norma proíbe ainda o uso de deepfake para favorecer ou prejudicar candidaturas, mesmo quando há autorização da pessoa cuja imagem ou voz foi recriada.
A eventual irregularidade dependerá de provocação e julgamento da Justiça Eleitoral. Politicamente, porém, a função da peça foi inequívoca: devolver voz eleitoral a Jair Bolsonaro e usar sua imagem para transferir apoio ao filho. Impedido de aparecer, telefonar, publicar ou mandar recados por aliados, o ex-presidente subiu ao palanque como personagem fabricado por computador.

DCM.titulo: Milei chama Lula de “presidiário” e Moraes de “lixo careca” em convenção de Flávio Bolsonaro
DCM.resumoOriginal:
Milei na convenção do PL em SP com Flávio Bolsonaro
O presidente da Argentina, Javier Milei, transformou a convenção do Partido Liberal (PL), realizada neste sábado (25), em São Paulo, em um palanque de ataques ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, ao ministro Alexandre de Moraes, à esquerda latino-americana e às instituições brasileiras.
Principal convidado do evento que oficializou a candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro à Presidência da República, o argentino afirmou confiar no senador para “parar Lula” e derrotar o que chamou de “socialismo da pobreza”.
Em um discurso de cerca de 30 minutos, o presidente argentino classificou Lula como um “presidiário” e disse que o kirchnerismo representa, na Argentina, uma versão do modelo político liderado pelo petista.
“O kirchnerismo é a versão argentina do presidiário”, afirmou Milei, ao associar Lula ao legado de Fidel Castro e acusar governos de esquerda de espalharem pobreza e autoritarismo pela América Latina.
Segundo Milei, apenas Flávio Bolsonaro seria capaz de interromper esse processo no Brasil. “Eu creio que somente Flávio pode parar Lula e trazer uma verdadeira mudança para todos os brasileiros. Confio plenamente nele para enfrentar o socialismo, o crime organizado e o narcotráfico”, disse.

🚨AGORA – Milei acaba de fazer sua entrada na convenção que vai oficializar a candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro pic.twitter.com/cw5rheonS6
— SPACE LIBERDADE  (@NewsLiberdade) July 25, 2026
Alexandre de Moraes é chamado de “lixo careca”
O presidente argentino também atacou diretamente o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal, por não ter autorizado uma visita ao ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, que cumpre prisão domiciliar.
Chamando Bolsonaro de “grande amigo”, Milei afirmou que foi impedido de encontrá-lo e se referiu a Moraes como “lixo careca”, arrancando aplausos da plateia.
Durante o discurso, o argentino ainda alertou Flávio Bolsonaro para o que chamou de uma disputa eleitoral dura. “Os esquerdistas vão jogar duro. Prepare-se para uma grande batalha”, falou.

🚨URGENTE – Milei fica revoltado por não permitirem sua visita a Bolsonaro e detona Lula
“Não me permitiram visitar meu amigo injustamente preso! Lula se cansou de receber pessoas do exterior quando estava preso!” pic.twitter.com/DjTg2bg4V6
— SPACE LIBERDADE  (@NewsLiberdade) July 25, 2026

Em diversos momentos da fala, apoiadores presentes na Arena Pacaembu puxaram o coro de “Lula ladrão, seu lugar é na prisão”. Milei reagiu incentivando os manifestantes, fazendo gestos para que aumentassem o volume dos gritos e balançando a cabeça em sinal de aprovação.
Ao longo da apresentação, o presidente argentino voltou a defender sua agenda econômica liberal, repetiu críticas ao socialismo e afirmou que espera ver o Brasil seguir o mesmo caminho adotado por seu governo.
Tarcísio recebe Milei antes da convenção
Antes do evento partidário, Milei foi recebido pelo governador de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas, no Palácio dos Bandeirantes. Na ocasião, recebeu a Ordem do Ipiranga, a mais alta honraria concedida pelo Estado de São Paulo.

Javier Milei 🦁🇦🇷 puxa o coro: “Lula Ladrão, seu lugar é na prisão!”. Milei convida Flávio para destruir o socialismo e o Foro de São Paulo na América Latina.
Viva la libertad, carajo! 🇧🇷🇦🇷 pic.twitter.com/Hx6R8JcL0f
— Thom 🇧🇷 🔪 (@94tome14) July 25, 2026
Também participaram do encontro o prefeito Ricardo Nunes e o próprio Flávio Bolsonaro.
A convenção do PL oficializou a candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro à Presidência da República nas eleições de outubro. O senador tenta consolidar sua candidatura em meio às dificuldades para ampliar alianças partidárias e herda a liderança do grupo político após a inelegibilidade e a prisão domiciliar de Jair Bolsonaro.
Mesmo ausente, Michelle Bolsonaro participou por meio de uma mensagem gravada em vídeo. Na gravação, desejou sucesso ao senador e pediu proteção divina para sua campanha, em uma rara demonstração pública de apoio após semanas de atritos internos na família Bolsonaro.

🚨URGENTE – Milei diz que o Foro de São Paulo foi criado por Lula para disseminar o comunismo na região
“O infame Foro de SP foi criado por Lula e Fidel Castro pra disseminar o comunismo no continente” pic.twitter.com/tx03Bn7Lwp
— SPACE LIBERDADE  (@NewsLiberdade) July 25, 2026

DCM.titulo: VÍDEO: Nikolas mente e dá balão em Flávio Bolsonaro
DCM.resumoOriginal:
O pré-candidato a presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) e o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG). Foto: Beto Barata/PL
Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) não compareceu neste sábado (25) à convenção nacional do PL que oficializou Flávio Bolsonaro como candidato à Presidência. Ao lado do deputado Domingos Sávio (PL-MG) e de um piloto, ele gravou um vídeo mentindo, dizendo que sua ausência foi causado pelo mau tempo em São Paulo e a dificuldades para pousar em Guarulhos.
“Tava aqui já com o uniforme pronto para a convenção”, afirmou Nikolas. O piloto disse que as condições meteorológicas no início da manhã teriam impedido a viagem e que uma tentativa de obter autorização para Guarulhos esbarrou no pátio lotado e no tempo necessário para o deslocamento terrestre.
Os registros públicos da aviação mostram um quadro menos dramático. Guarulhos teve neblina, nuvens baixas e visibilidade reduzida durante a manhã, mas não houve fechamento geral do aeroporto. Por volta das 11h, a visibilidade era de 4,5 quilômetros, com vento de apenas dois nós. As condições permitiam operações por instrumentos.
Também não há registro público que confirme a alegada lotação do pátio de Guarulhos. O aeroporto continuava operando, e os sistemas oficiais não indicavam paralisação, contingência ou saturação extraordinária.
Em Congonhas, o cenário já era mais favorável. Os boletins indicavam visibilidade acima de dez quilômetros, vento fraco e operações programadas ao longo do dia. Os dados não sustentam a ideia de que os aeroportos de São Paulo estivessem, de maneira geral, sem condições de receber voos.

Nikolas Ferreira não vai à convenção do PL por mau tempo, mas grava vídeo de apoio a Flávio
O deputado Nikolas Ferreira não participará da Convenção Nacional do PL por não conseguir se deslocar até São Paulo devido ao mau tempo. Assim como Michelle Bolsonaro, ele gravou um vídeo… pic.twitter.com/fy9gcMLVnC
— Pesquisas Eleições (@EleicaoBr2026) July 25, 2026

Os dados oficiais provam a mentira que o piloto e Nikolas tentam emplacar. A própria fala revela que a tentativa de autorização ocorreu “muito próximo do horário”. Em Guarulhos, voos de aviação geral precisam de autorização e coordenação prévias, com antecedência mínima de seis ou 24 horas, conforme a categoria da aeronave.
Em Congonhas, a coordenação deve ocorrer ao menos duas horas antes. Portanto, uma eventual negativa de pouso apontaria para improviso ou falha de planejamento da viagem, não para uma impossibilidade provocada pelo clima.
Nikolas mentiu ao transformar sua falta de planejamento em uma desculpa mal contato para não subir ao palanque de Flávio Bolsonaro.
Politicamente, porém, a ausência foi conveniente para um aliado que mantém relação instável com a campanha de Flávio. Segundo levantamento, Nikolas havia citado o senador em somente dez das 544 postagens que fez no X desde o lançamento da pré-candidatura. Ele chegou a ser cobrado publicamente por integrantes da família Bolsonaro por falta de empenho.
Nikolas e Domingos Sávio apoiaram Flávio pelo telão, sem pisar na convenção. Michelle Bolsonaro também ficou em Brasília e enviou somente um vídeo. No lançamento da candidatura, faltaram a principal liderança feminina do bolsonarismo, o deputado mais popular do PL nas redes e o presidente do partido em Minas.
A cena lembra, com as diferenças necessárias, outro mineiro resistente a embarcar em uma candidatura nacional. Em 2010, Aécio Neves recusava a pressão para ser vice de José Serra e repetiu uma frase atribuída ao avô, Tancredo Neves: “Não adianta empurrar, empurrado eu não vou”. Aécio assumiu abertamente a recusa; Nikolas diz que tentou viajar. Nos dois casos, o apoio foi mantido a uma distância politicamente segura.

DCM.titulo: Trump cobra tarifa maior do Brasil e dá isenções extras a 13 concorrentes
DCM.resumoOriginal:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. Foto: Molly Riley/Casa Branca
O governo de Donald Trump colocou os exportadores brasileiros em uma segunda camada de desvantagem no mercado dos Estados Unidos. Além de cobrar do Brasil a alíquota integral de 12,5%, Washington concedeu listas adicionais de produtos isentos a 13 economias concorrentes.
O Brasil não ficou totalmente fora das exceções. Uma relação comum de cerca de 2,1 mil códigos de produtos vale para o país e dezenas de outros mercados investigados. A diferença é que Argentina, Reino Unido, União Europeia, Malásia e outros parceiros receberam listas exclusivas, elaboradas conforme os compromissos assumidos com o governo estadunidense.
A Argentina ganhou 93 exceções adicionais, segundo levantamento feito a partir dos anexos da decisão. A Malásia recebeu 105; o Reino Unido, 49; e a União Europeia, 43. O tratamento favorecido inclui categorias de madeira processada, equipamentos hospitalares, produtos químicos, óleos vegetais e insumos naturais.
O efeito pode ser particularmente forte sobre a madeira brasileira destinada à construção civil estadunidense. Argentina e Equador tiveram diferentes categorias do produto poupadas, enquanto itens equivalentes exportados pelo Brasil continuam sujeitos à cobrança. Pedras preciosas, diamantes, esmeraldas, próteses médicas e leveduras também aparecem entre os segmentos expostos à perda de competitividade.
Vista aérea do Porto de Santos (SP). Foto: Jorge Silva/Reuters
O economista Sergio Vale, da MB Associados, calcula que os produtos brasileiros diretamente prejudicados pelas exceções concedidas aos concorrentes representam 3,4% da pauta atingida pela tarifa de 12,5%. As vendas somam aproximadamente US$ 470 milhões.
A diferença se torna maior nos itens também alcançados pela tarifa de 25% imposta especificamente ao Brasil em outra investigação comercial. Nesses casos, as sobretaxas podem chegar a 37,5%, contra 10% cobrados de parceiros como Argentina, Malásia e Reino Unido. A distância máxima é de 27,5 pontos percentuais, sem considerar a tarifa normal de cada mercadoria.
A justificativa de Washington não é que esses produtos brasileiros tenham sido fabricados com trabalho forçado. O USTR afirma que o Brasil não possui uma lei equivalente à Seção 307 dos Estados Unidos, que proíbe expressamente a importação de mercadorias produzidas total ou parcialmente nessas condições em outros países.
A legislação comercial estadunidense permite, porém, que as sanções sejam aplicadas mesmo a mercadorias e setores sem relação direta com a prática investigada. Na prática, produtos brasileiros sem qualquer acusação de trabalho forçado passam a pagar mais, enquanto concorrentes escolhidos por Washington recebem tarifas menores e exceções próprias.

DCM.titulo: VÍDEO: Livre na Itália, Zambelli volta ao X e divulga candidatura da mãe a deputada
DCM.resumoOriginal:
Carla Zambelli falando para a câmera em vídeo nas redes sociais. Foto: Reprodução
A ex-deputada federal Carla Zambelli voltou ao X após deixar a prisão na Itália e usou um vídeo para avisar que retomará a comunicação direta com seus seguidores durante a campanha eleitoral.
No mesmo vídeo, Zambelli divulgou a candidatura da mãe, Rita Zambelli (PL-SP), que deve disputar uma vaga na Câmara dos Deputados por São Paulo. Durante o período em que a ex-parlamentar ficou presa, Rita administrava as redes sociais da filha.
“Volto para minhas redes e vamos conversar durante toda essa campanha. Muita coisa tem para acontecer. Nós temos que falar do que está acontecendo de errado no Brasil e temos que apontar qual é o caminho, qual é a solução. E a solução passa, obviamente, pela eleição”, disse Zambelli.

Que saudade de vocês! Gostaria muito de agradecer pelo carinho e apoio que deram a mim e a minha família neste período tão difícil
Peço que, com o mesmo carinho, sigam minha mãe @RITAZAMBELLI, minha voz, minha pré-candidata a deputada federal por SP pelo @plnacional_
Amo vocês pic.twitter.com/5aTk8TQBct
— Carla Zambelli (@ZambelliCarla_) July 25, 2026

Condenações no Brasil e pedido de extradição na Itália
A ex-deputada está na Itália enquanto o governo brasileiro tenta obter sua extradição. No Brasil, ela recebeu condenações em dois processos distintos, com penas relacionadas a invasão hacker e a porte ilegal de arma de fogo.
Em 22 de maio, a Corte de Cassação de Roma, última instância da Justiça italiana, anulou uma decisão de instância inferior que havia autorizado a extradição de Zambelli no caso da invasão ao sistema do Conselho Nacional de Justiça.
Nesse processo, a Justiça brasileira condenou Zambelli a 10 anos e 8 meses de prisão como autora intelectual do crime. A decisão italiana sobre a extradição tratava especificamente desse caso ligado ao CNJ.
Desde a anulação da decisão que autorizava a extradição no caso do CNJ, Zambelli permanece em liberdade na Itália. O retorno ao X ocorreu depois dessa mudança na situação dela no país europeu.
Na outra condenação, de 5 anos e 3 meses de prisão por porte ilegal de arma de fogo e perseguição armada, a Suprema Corte italiana determinou o reinício do processo, que voltará a ser analisado por uma instância inferior.

DCM.titulo: Estagiária é presa sob suspeita de espionagem na Otan
DCM.resumoOriginal:
Militar faz segurança da cúpula da Otan em Haia, em 24 de junho de 2025. Foto: Reprodução
Uma cidadã canadense de origem chinesa foi presa na Bélgica sob suspeita de espionagem enquanto atuava como estagiária na sede militar da Organização do Tratado do Atlântico Norte (Otan), informou a Promotoria Federal belga no sábado (25).
A Promotoria não informou para qual país a suspeita teria repassado informações. As autoridades também não divulgaram o nome da mulher.
A estagiária trabalhava no Quartel-General Supremo das Potências Aliadas na Europa, conhecido pela sigla SHAPE. A instalação fica em uma cidade no sul da Bélgica.
Os serviços de segurança do SHAPE identificaram indícios de espionagem e comunicaram o caso ao Serviço Geral de Inteligência e Segurança da Bélgica, que encaminhou a investigação às autoridades judiciais.
Quartel-General Supremo das Potências Aliadas na Europa (Shape), na cidade de Mons.
Buscas e prisão preventiva na Bélgica
A Polícia Judiciária Federal abriu uma investigação após receber o caso das autoridades de inteligência belgas.
Na quinta-feira (23), agentes realizaram buscas na casa da suspeita e no escritório onde ela trabalhava dentro da estrutura ligada à Otan.
Na sexta-feira (24), uma juíza de instrução decretou a prisão preventiva da mulher pelos crimes de espionagem e participação em organização criminosa.
A Promotoria Federal belga afirmou que não divulgará novos detalhes para não comprometer o andamento das investigações.

DCM.titulo: Lula abre 5,6 pontos sobre Flávio Bolsonaro em agregador com Quaest e Datafolha
DCM.resumoOriginal:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e Flávio Bolsonaro em composição com fotos oficiais. Foto: Reprodução
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) aparece 5,6 pontos percentuais à frente do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) em uma simulação de segundo turno do agregador de pesquisas Rali, iniciativa do GLOBO em parceria com o Instituto Locomotiva.
No cenário agregado, Lula tem 46,5% das intenções de voto, contra 40,9% de Flávio. A diferença foi ampliada após as rodadas mais recentes dos levantamentos Datafolha e Genial/Quaest, divulgadas em julho.
Em junho, o petista registrava 45% no mesmo recorte, enquanto o bolsonarista marcava 40,6%. Naquele momento, a vantagem de Lula era de 4,4 pontos percentuais.
O movimento contrasta com o quadro de maio. No dia 5 daquele mês, Flávio aparecia numericamente à frente, com 44,4%, contra 43,7% de Lula. Em meados de maio, os dois estavam empatados no agregador, com 43,8% cada.
Pesquisa Datafolha. Foto: Reprodução/DCM
Datafolha aponta Lula à frente nos cenários de segundo turno
A pesquisa Datafolha divulgada na sexta-feira (24) colocou Lula na liderança de todos os cenários de segundo turno testados pelo instituto.
Na simulação direta contra Flávio Bolsonaro, o Datafolha apontou o presidente com 48% das intenções de voto. O senador apareceu com 43% no mesmo confronto.
Flávio é tratado pelo PL como pré-candidato ao Palácio do Planalto. A disputa projetada pelo Rali mede um confronto direto entre o atual presidente e o senador, filho de Jair Bolsonaro.
Em outro recorte do Datafolha, Flávio Bolsonaro aparece com 48% de rejeição, enquanto Lula registra 46% nesse indicador.

DCM.titulo: VÍDEO – Milei se encontra com Flávio Bolsonaro antes da convenção do PL
DCM.resumoOriginal:
Javier Milei e Flávio Bolsonaro lado a lado em encontro divulgado nas redes sociais. Foto: Reprodução
O presidente da Argentina, Javier Milei, declarou apoio ao senador e pré-candidato à Presidência da República Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) neste sábado (25), antes da convenção nacional do Partido Liberal que oficializará o nome do parlamentar na disputa pelo Palácio do Planalto.
Flávio se reuniu com Milei, o governador de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), e o prefeito da capital paulista, Ricardo Nunes (MDB). O encontro ocorreu antes do evento partidário do PL.
Nas redes sociais, o senador publicou um registro da reunião e afirmou que os quatro defendem uma agenda comum. “Hoje estive ao lado do presidente da Argentina, Javier Milei, do governador de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas, e do prefeito de São Paulo, Ricardo Nunes. Quatro lideranças, um compromisso: menos burocracia, mais liberdade e respeito ao dinheiro do povo”, escreveu.
Durante a conversa, os participantes trataram de redução da burocracia, liberdade econômica e responsabilidade na gestão dos recursos públicos. A presença de Milei no evento do PL marca nova aproximação pública entre o presidente argentino e o grupo político liderado por Flávio.

🇧🇷🇦🇷 ATENÇÃO: Ao lado de Tarcísio, Flávio Bolsonaro se reúne com Javier Milei no Palácio dos Bandeirantes.
O presidente argentino participará da convenção que oficializará a candidatura de Flávio à Presidência, no Pacaembu.
🎥 @FlavioBolsonaro pic.twitter.com/mmT6DhR9uo
— Central da Direita 🇧🇷 (@CentralDireitaB) July 25, 2026

Milei lamenta veto a encontro com Jair Bolsonaro
Milei também comentou a impossibilidade de visitar o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL). “É uma pena que não pude ver teu pai”, afirmou o argentino a Flávio durante o encontro.
O ministro Alexandre de Moraes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), negou no último sábado (18) o pedido da defesa de Jair Bolsonaro para que ele recebesse Milei em Brasília. A visita estava prevista para este sábado (25).
Flávio respondeu ao presidente argentino dizendo que ele terá novas oportunidades de ir ao Brasil. “Mas logo você voltará. Firmes para a onda azul chegar ao Brasil”, declarou o senador.
Na sequência, Milei associou sua presença à campanha do PL e falou em expectativa para a eleição. “Obviamente, viemos acompanhar a onda azul. Eu digo que é a hora, é uma grande esperança para outubro”, disse o presidente da Argentina.

Democracy Now!.titulo: "Farmers of the Sea": PBS Film Profiles Puerto Rican Fishermen on the "Frontlines of Climate Change"
Democracy Now!.resumoOriginal: Filmmaker Juan Carlos Dávila’s new film for PBS, Farmers of the Sea, documents climate change’s threats to the fishing industry and food security in Vieques, Puerto Rico. For islands in the Caribbean, explains Dávila, “we are situated geographically in one of the frontlines of climate change. [We’re] not only facing stronger hurricanes now, [but] we could face food shortages, especially the islands that depend so much on the food that comes from the sea.”

Democracy Now!.titulo: Report from San Juan: New Bill Targets Citizenship Rights as Puerto Rico Marks 10 Years of PROMESA
Democracy Now!.resumoOriginal:
After failing to overturn birthright citizenship at the Supreme Court, Republican legislators are turning to new tactics to disenfranchise people born on U.S. soil. Their latest targets are those born to noncitizen or permanent resident parents in U.S. territories like Puerto Rico, where the Supreme Court has said citizenship is granted by statute and full constitutional protections do not apply. The proposed “End Birthright Citizenship for the Territories Act” would create “a subclass of people who can be discriminated against” and “disregarded as human beings” in the U.S. territories, says Puerto Rican legal scholar Efrén Rivera Ramos, who joins Democracy Now! from Puerto Rico’s capital city, San Juan. While the bill’s sponsor, Republican Congressmember Morgan Griffith of Virginia, says he’s focused only on so-called birth tourism, Rivera Ramos says the language of the law is less clear.
The quasi-colonial status of Puerto Rico is also being highlighted by the 10th anniversary of PROMESA, the Obama-era legislation that created a U.S.-appointed fiscal control board to manage the island’s finances and restructure debt. In practice, PROMESA “has been a failure,” says Rivera Ramos, asserting the anti-democratic structure has imposed austerity measures and done little to address corruption, waste and inefficiency that plague the economy.

Democracy Now!.titulo: "Cockroach Democracy": Arundhati Roy on India's Youth-Led Protest Movement & Modi's Collapsing Support
Democracy Now!.resumoOriginal: A youth-led protest movement in India is demanding an end to the country’s status quo. Sparked by the leak of national exam questions, tens of thousands of young people have taken to the streets. They are protesting under the banner of the Cockroach Janta (People’s) Party — a new party named to reflect the words of India’s chief justice, who compared unemployed youth to cockroaches and parasites. The movement has only swelled in response to a violent crackdown on protesters. Although the protesters’ initial demands were for the resignation of the country’s education minister, “everything has shifted to directly attacking [Prime Minister Narendra] Modi,” says Indian writer Arundhati Roy, who joins us from New Delhi, the physical center of a movement that first found exponential success online. The erosion of democratic principles under Modi’s right-wing Bharatiya Janata (Indian People’s) Party is being contested on a large scale for the first time, says Roy. “It’s really a generation whose parents and grandparents wore those Modi masks and chanted 'Modi, Modi, Modi,' and got him into power. It is their children now who are saying the emperor has no clothes.”

Democracy Now!.titulo: "America First or Israel First?" Ex-Israeli Negotiator Daniel Levy on Saudi Nuclear Deal, Iran & More
Democracy Now!.resumoOriginal:
The status of a newly signed U.S.-Saudi nuclear deal is in question after President Trump made the surprise announcement that the deal is off unless Saudi Arabia normalizes relations with Israel. The deal paves the way for Saudi civil nuclear development, although critics warn that it could lead to the proliferation of nuclear weapons in the politically volatile Middle East.
Saudi Arabia has long maintained that it would not officially recognize Israel by joining the Abraham Accords, the U.S.-negotiated diplomatic deal between Israel and a number of Arab states, until there is a pathway toward the creation of a Palestinian state. The Abraham Accords provision indicates that “Israel is calling the shots again,” when it comes to U.S. policy in the Middle East, notes Daniel Levy of the U.S./Middle East Project. Levy says it is unlikely that Saudi Arabia will agree to Trump’s new conditions, at a cost to U.S. business interests, which stand to profit handily from the sale of nuclear energy technology to the oil-rich kingdom.

Democracy Now!.titulo: As Mamdani Calls on Trump to Arrest Netanyahu, Genocide Scholar Decries Israel's Ongoing Impunity
Democracy Now!.resumoOriginal:
Israeli American Holocaust scholar Omer Bartov says Israel’s assault on Gaza predicts “the future of genocide,” with the perpetrator not only enjoying impunity for crimes against humanity but also profiting from the death and destruction. He says Israeli leaders will almost certainly escape accountability because international allies, including the United States and many European states, have failed to uphold international law.
“The denial of what Israel has done is ubiquitous because there is no [accountability] mechanism that kicks into place,” he says. “If you don’t bring people to account, you’re sliding back into what the international community tried to prevent after 1945.”

Democracy Now!.titulo: "Enough Is Enough": Mohsen Mahdawi Says New Deportation Threat Seeks to Silence Palestine Activism
Meet Milwaukee Muslim Leader Salah Sarsour. ICE Detained Him for 80 Days
Democracy Now!.resumoOriginal:
We speak with Salah Sarsour, a Palestinian community leader in Wisconsin, president of the Islamic Society of Milwaukee and a legal permanent resident of the United States for over 30 years. He faces possible deportation after being arrested in March and detained in an ICE jail for 80 days. The Department of Homeland Security claims Sarsour was arrested for lying on his 1993 green card application about a conviction in Israeli military courts when he was a teenager in the occupied West Bank, but Sarsour’s lawyers say he is being targeted by the federal government over his advocacy for Palestinian human rights. Although a judge ordered Sarsour’s release from detention in June, he still faces deportation proceedings set to resume next week.
“In ICE detention,” says Sarsour, “it brought to me these bad memories from my childhood, when I was under the Israeli military occupation and Israeli military rules in Palestine.”
